editorial.headline: Pig Slaughterhouse Operations, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10112 covers pig slaughterhouse work, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali PMA block under the record’s current risk reading.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 10112 is the business of operating a pig slaughterhouse.** The record defines it around the physical slaughterhouse sequence: slaughtering pigs, including wild pigs, then skinning, cleaning, and packing the meat. It is not written as a general meat-trading category or a broad food-service activity. Its centre of gravity is the controlled handling of animals and meat at the slaughter point, plus the immediate preparation that turns the slaughtered animal into packed meat.

The scope also reaches the less visible side of the slaughterhouse: the management of by-products. The record includes the production of hides and skins from slaughterhouses and farms or fellmongery, drying bones, processing animal remnants or waste, and cleaning fat. That matters because this code is not only about the main cut of meat leaving the facility. It captures the full industrial logic of the slaughterhouse floor, including the materials and residues generated by the work itself.

On scale, the record is unusually clear: this activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators. In practical editorial terms, the code is not reserved in the record for only one size of enterprise. A small operator and a larger facility both sit within the same activity description, provided the registered business is truly doing the slaughterhouse and associated handling described in the scope. The wording supports a business model built around slaughtering, cleaning, packing, and by-product management, rather than a model that merely buys and sells meat elsewhere.

The national foreign-investment position is also direct. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with `pma_max_asing` at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. So the national reading is full foreign ownership: 100%. The Bali-side picture does not reverse that in this record. The Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`, `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule still matters because Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this record does not place KBLI 10112 inside that block. The honest reading is therefore clean: nationally foreign-open, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record’s stated Bali risk rationale.
